planting.note: Start seed indoors after nicking or sanding the hard seed coat, and only move seedlings outdoors once nights stay reliably above the mid-40s F.

directions: Toromiro is a small, multi-stemmed legume tree with fine, silvery pinnate foliage and small yellow pea-shaped flowers, once the only native tree on Easter Island and now extinct in its natural habitat. Its survival depends entirely on ex-situ seed stocks maintained by botanic gardens such as Gothenburg Botanical Garden, which have periodically made seed available to outside growers and specialist rare-plant seed vendors. Give it lean, sharply drained soil, full sun, and protection from hard frost, since it comes from a mild subtropical island climate and will not tolerate prolonged cold or wet conditions. Treat any seed you obtain as precious: scarify the hard outer coat to improve germination, and expect slow, steady growth into a modest flowering tree over several years.
sources: Gothenburg Botanical Garden toromiro conservation program
